title: Asset Recovery: Tracing, Freezing and Confiscation
summary: An eight-module programme equipping practitioners to trace, restrain, confiscate, manage and return criminal assets, including crypto-assets and assets held abroad.
intro: This training programme equips investigators, prosecutors and asset recovery practitioners to trace, restrain, confiscate and manage criminal assets, using conviction-based and non-conviction-based routes at home and across borders.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give practitioners a complete view of the asset recovery cycle, from identifying and tracing assets to freezing, confiscation, management and final disposal or return. Participants leave able to choose the right legal route, act early to prevent dissipation, manage assets to preserve value and pursue assets held abroad or as crypto-assets.
sections.What It Covers: The asset recovery cycle and international standards, conviction-based and non-conviction-based confiscation, unexplained wealth and civil routes, identifying and tracing assets, freezing and restraint, asset management and realisation, international requests and cooperation, crypto-assets, and disposal, victim compensation and the return of assets.
Intended Audience: Asset recovery officers, financial investigators and asset recovery office staff
Prosecutors and lawyers handling restraint, confiscation and civil recovery proceedings
Asset management office staff and customs, tax and FIU officers involved in recovering criminal proceeds
Learning Objectives: Explain the asset recovery cycle and the international standards that frame it
Select the most effective legal route, whether conviction-based or non-conviction-based
Trace and value assets held directly, through third parties and in corporate vehicles
Apply freezing and restraint early and proportionately to prevent dissipation
Manage restrained assets to preserve value and control cost
Pursue assets abroad and in crypto-assets, and plan for disposal, compensation and return
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a technical briefing with worked cases and legal-route exercises, ending in a recovery strategy workshop, and modules can be selected or tailored to the national legal framework.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial investigation, prosecution or asset recovery work is helpful. No legal qualification is required.
Core Reading: World Bank and UNODC StAR Initiative (2021), Asset Recovery Handbook: A Guide for Practitioners, Second Edition
World Bank and UNODC StAR Initiative (2009), Stolen Asset Recovery: A Good Practices Guide for Non-Conviction Based Asset Forfeiture
FATF (2012), Best Practices on Confiscation (Recommendations 4 and 38) and a Framework for Ongoing Work on Asset Recovery
UNODC (2012), Manual on International Cooperation for the Purposes of Confiscation of Proceeds of Crime

modules.title: Asset Recovery: Cycle, Standards and Strategy
modules.summary: Why recovering criminal assets matters, the stages of the asset recovery cycle, and the international standards and conventions that set expectations for national regimes.
objectives: Explain the purposes and stages of asset recovery
Summarise the FATF standards and the relevant international conventions
Set an asset recovery strategy at the start of a case
syllabus: The cycle: identification, tracing, freezing, confiscation, management and disposal
FATF Recommendations 4 and 38 and Immediate Outcome 8
International conventions against corruption and organised crime
Asset recovery strategies, priorities and institutional models

modules.title: Legal Routes: Conviction-Based and Non-Conviction-Based
modules.summary: The main legal routes to recover criminal assets, including object- and value-based confiscation, extended confiscation, non-conviction-based forfeiture and unexplained wealth tools, and how to choose between them.
objectives: Compare conviction-based, non-conviction-based and civil recovery routes
Explain object-based, value-based and extended confiscation
Choose the most effective route for the facts and evidence
syllabus: Object-based and value-based confiscation and benefit calculation
Extended confiscation and shifting the burden of proof
Non-conviction-based forfeiture, civil recovery and unexplained wealth tools
Safeguards: proportionality, third-party rights and fair trial

modules.title: Identifying and Tracing Assets
modules.summary: How practitioners locate and trace assets held directly, through family members and associates, in corporate vehicles or abroad, and build an asset profile that supports restraint.
objectives: Build an asset profile from registers, records and intelligence
Trace assets through third parties, structures and jurisdictions
Value assets and identify competing interests
syllabus: Asset profiling: property, accounts, vehicles, businesses and high-value goods
Tracing through nominees, associates and corporate vehicles
Asset recovery office networks and international enquiries
Valuation, encumbrances and third-party claims

modules.title: Freezing, Seizure and Restraint
modules.summary: How and when to secure assets before they are dissipated, the evidential thresholds for restraint, and how to draft and manage orders that are proportionate and enforceable.
objectives: Explain the thresholds and procedure for freezing, seizure and restraint
Draft proportionate, enforceable restraint applications
Manage variations, living expenses and third-party challenges
syllabus: Timing: risk of dissipation and acting early
Administrative freezes, seizure and court restraint orders
Drafting applications and supporting statements
Variations, legal expenses, third parties and discharge

modules.title: Asset Management and Realisation
modules.summary: How restrained and confiscated assets are managed to preserve value, the role of asset management offices and receivers, and the options for interim sale and final realisation.
objectives: Plan before seizure for the management of complex assets
Assess options for preserving value, including interim sale
Oversee receivers, custodians and asset management offices
syllabus: Pre-seizure planning: businesses, property, vehicles and perishable assets
Asset management offices, receivers and custodians
Interim sale, valuation and cost control
Realisation, enforcement of orders and dealing with default

modules.title: International Requests and Cooperation
modules.summary: How to identify, freeze and recover assets held abroad through informal cooperation, mutual legal assistance and recognition of foreign orders, and how to make requests that succeed.
objectives: Use informal networks before making formal requests
Draft mutual legal assistance requests for tracing, freezing and confiscation
Explain the recognition and enforcement of foreign orders
syllabus: Informal cooperation: asset recovery networks, FIUs and liaison officers
Mutual legal assistance requests: content, evidence and timing
Recognition of foreign freezing and confiscation orders
Common obstacles and how to overcome them

modules.title: Crypto-Assets and Other Emerging Assets
modules.summary: How to identify, seize, hold and realise crypto-assets and other emerging asset types, working with service providers and maintaining secure custody and continuity.
objectives: Identify indicators of crypto-asset holdings during an investigation
Explain secure seizure, custody and realisation of crypto-assets
Work with service providers to freeze and recover funds
syllabus: Indicators of crypto-asset holdings: devices, records and statements
Seizure approaches: private keys, service providers and custody solutions
Valuation volatility, conversion and realisation
Other emerging assets: tokenised assets and online accounts

modules.title: Disposal, Return and Recovery Strategy: Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together by examining victim compensation, return of assets across borders and social reuse, ending with a workshop in which teams build a recovery strategy for a complex case.
objectives: Explain the options for compensation, return and disposal of recovered assets
Apply principles of transparent and accountable asset return
Design an end-to-end recovery strategy for a realistic case
syllabus: Victim compensation and restitution
Principles for the transparent and accountable return of assets
Asset sharing, social reuse and funding models
Workshop: a recovery strategy from tracing to return

related.title: Financial Investigation: Following the Money
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping investigators and analysts to run parallel financial investigations, trace funds through accounts and corporate vehicles, and present financial evidence.

related.title: FIU Operational and Strategic Analysis
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping FIU analysts to prioritise and analyse reports, produce operational and strategic intelligence, and cooperate effectively at home and abroad.

related.title: Fraud and Cyber-Enabled Financial Crime Investigations
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping investigators and FIU analysts to tackle fraud, money mules and ransomware proceeds, working with banks and payment firms to recover funds.

related.title: Prosecuting Financial Crime: Evidence, Experts and the Courtroom
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping prosecutors and judges to handle money laundering and complex financial crime cases, from charge and evidence to sentencing and confiscation.

related.title: Public-Private Partnerships and Financial Intelligence Sharing
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping FIUs and law-enforcement agencies to design, run and evaluate public-private partnerships for sharing financial intelligence lawfully and effectively.

related.title: Tax Crime and Money Laundering
related.summary: A six-module programme equipping tax, FIU and law-enforcement investigators to tackle tax crime and related laundering through information exchange and joint investigation.
